summary: IGP Flexible Algorithm computes constrained paths using administrative policy. This document adds an extension that includes or excludes links based on reverse affinity, using link attributes seen from the opposite direction. It updates RFC 9350 and RFC 9843.

eli5.summary: A road can be fine one way and bad the other. This lets path planning take the road's rating in the reverse direction into account.

questions: what is a reverse admin group

subtitle: Lets Flex-Algorithm prune links using the Admin Groups set on the reverse direction of a link.

tldr.problem: Flex-Algorithm checks link Admin Groups only in the direction of the path computation, so problems visible only at the far end of a link, such as input errors, cannot be used to exclude that link.
tldr.mechanism: Three new sub-TLVs per protocol (exclude, include-any, include-all) carry reverse Admin Group rules in the Flexible Algorithm Definition, and three new pruning rules check the Admin Groups set on the reverse-direction edge.
tldr.outcome: Operators can steer traffic away from a link based on conditions detected at its far end. The RFC also creates an IANA registry of ordered path computation rules, and it updates RFC 9350 and RFC 9843.

today: RFC 9917 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2026. It updates RFC 9350 and RFC 9843, and the metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated itself.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
IGPs historically computed best paths using only the IGP metric on links. An IGP Flex-Algorithm, specified in RFC 9350, allows constraint-based paths. Existing constraints include link inclusion or exclusion by Admin Group, exclusion by Shared Risk Link Group (SRLG), exclusion based on minimum bandwidth and exclusion based on maximum delay (the last two from RFC 9843).

This document adds constraints that include or exclude links based on Admin Groups associated with the reverse direction of the Shortest Path First (SPF) computation. It also updates RFC 9350 and RFC 9843 by creating a new IANA registry for the ordered set of rules that prune links. The term OSPF here covers both OSPFv2 and OSPFv3.
sections.eli5: Until now, path planning only looked at a road's rating in the direction you were traveling. This RFC adds a check of the rating on the way back too.

sections.title: The Use Case
sections.content:
The Flexible Algorithm Definition (FAD) can name Extended Administrative Groups that include or exclude links. Normally these are checked in the path direction, from the root toward vertices of increasing distance.

Consider a point-to-point link as two directed edges between nodes A and B. When computing a path from A to B, input errors that only node B can detect may matter. An operator might watch Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) errors at B and, when a threshold is exceeded over an observation period, have B assign Extended Administrative Groups to the link in the B to A direction.

The Flex-Algorithm can then inspect the reverse edge (B to A) while evaluating the forward edge (A to B). This excludes links based on conditions detected at the far end.
sections.eli5: Imagine the end of a hallway notices the floor is slippery, but the person at the start cannot tell. This lets the far end put up a sign that the planner reads for the whole hallway.

sections.title: Deployment Consideration
sections.content:
Setting Admin Groups from thresholds must be done with care, to avoid excessive flooding and constant Flex-Algorithm path recalculation.

One approach is to use two thresholds: a higher one to set the Extended Administrative Group on the link, and a lower one to unset it. The RFC also notes that many implementations throttle how fast an IS-IS LSP, or an OSPFv2 or OSPFv3 LSA, can be updated at the originator. That throttling can also keep frequent changes to the Admin Group from destabilizing receivers.
sections.eli5: If a sign flips on and off every second, everyone gets confused. Using one level to turn it on and a lower level to turn it off keeps it from flickering.

sections.title: The Reverse Admin Group Sub-TLVs
sections.content:
There are three new sub-TLVs for each protocol: Exclude Reverse Admin Group (FAERAG), Include-Any Reverse Admin Group and Include-All Reverse Admin Group. In IS-IS they are sub-TLVs of the IS-IS FAD Sub-TLV, with a 1-octet Type and 1-octet Length. In OSPF they are sub-TLVs of the OSPF FAD TLV, with a 2-octet Type and 2-octet Length. The Type values are 10, 11 and 12 respectively in both protocols.

The body is an Extended Administrative Group as defined in RFC 7308. The Length is variable and MUST be a multiple of 4 octets. Otherwise the receiver MUST ignore the entire sub-TLV.

Each sub-TLV MUST NOT appear more than once in a single FAD. If it does, the receiver MUST ignore the FAD. For IS-IS, if one appears more than once across the set of FAD Sub-TLVs for a Flex-Algorithm from one IS, the first occurrence in the lowest-numbered LSP is used and the others are ignored.
sections.eli5: Each rule is written on a small card with a type number and a length. The length has to come out in neat chunks of four, or the card gets thrown away.

sections.title: Calculating Flex-Algorithm Paths
sections.content:
The new procedures add to the rules in Section 13 of RFC 9350. Each looks at the Admin Groups set on the link in the reverse direction:

  • Exclude: if any Admin Group in the exclude reverse rule is set on the reverse link, the link MUST be pruned.
  • Include-any: if none of the Admin Groups in the rule is set on the reverse link, the link MUST be pruned.
  • Include-all: if not all of the Admin Groups in the rule are set on the reverse link, the link MUST be pruned.

These are rules 8, 9 and 10 in the new registry.
sections.eli5: For each road, look at the sign on the way back. If it has a banned label, skip the road. If you require a label and it is missing, skip the road too.

sections.title: IANA Registrations and the Rules Registry
sections.content:
IANA registered Types 10, 11 and 12 in the IS-IS Sub-Sub-TLVs for Flexible Algorithm Definition Sub-TLV registry and in the OSPF Flexible Algorithm Definition TLV Sub-TLVs registry.

IANA also created the IGP Flex-Algorithm Path Computation Rules registry, with Expert Review as the registration procedure and no upper bound on the number of rules. It lists, in order, the existing rules (1 to 5 from RFC 9350 and 6 and 7 from RFC 9843) and the three new ones (8 to 10). Guidance for designated experts: a new rule MAY be inserted at any position, because nodes that do not support a constraint will not take part in an algorithm whose FAD uses it. The relative order of existing rules MUST NOT be altered, rules MUST NOT be deleted, and rules MUST NOT be merged or repeated.
sections.eli5: There is now an official list of the checks, in order. New checks can be added, but old ones can never be removed or reshuffled.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document says only that it inherits the security considerations of RFC 9350 and adds no further text on the subject.
sections.eli5: It follows the same safety rules as the document it builds on and adds no new ones.

items.label: Exclude Reverse Admin Group
items.desc: Prune a link if any listed group is set on the reverse direction.

items.label: Include-Any Reverse Admin Group
items.desc: Prune a link unless at least one listed group is set on the reverse direction.

items.label: Include-All Reverse Admin Group
items.desc: Prune a link unless all listed groups are set on the reverse direction.

viz.caption: IS-IS REVERSE ADMIN GROUP SUB-TLV (1-OCTET TYPE AND LENGTH)

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: 10 for Exclude; 11 and 12 for the include variants.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Variable; MUST be a multiple of 4 octets.

fields.name: Extended Admin Group
fields.desc: Extended Administrative Group as defined in RFC 7308; the field continues in 4-octet units.
